speaker: A. W. Tozer
title: Prevenient grace and human pursuit
text: Before a man can seek God, God must first have sought the man. We pursue God because, and only because, He has first put an urge within us that spurs us to the pursuit. The impulse to pursue God originates with God, but the outworking of that impulse is our following hard after Him; and all the time we are pursuing Him we are already in His hand.
modern_interpretation: You don't just spontaneously decide to embark on a spiritual journey or seek deeper meaning; that profound longing, that inner nudge to connect with something greater, is actually a divine or universal impulse reaching out to you first. Your spiritual quest isn't merely your own initiative; it's a responsive journey to an innate calling placed within you, ensuring you are guided and held securely throughout the entire process.
summary: True spiritual seeking originates from a divine impulse placed within us, rather than our own initiative. We pursue God because He first ignites that urge, and during our pursuit, we remain continuously sustained by His grace and presence.
actionable_advice: Pay attention to those deep, persistent stirrings or yearnings for meaning, purpose, or spiritual connection, and trust that these internal prompts are a valid call to action, rather than just your own random thoughts.
